findings.diagnosis: The prompt demotes boundaries whose remainder would contradict the prefix, but it accomplishes this by promoting the immediately adjacent cut — producing one-word or head-fragment pieces (bare aux/copula, determiner-only, numeral-only, noun stripped of postmodifiers) that harm very-short latency bins.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_845','en_us_1116','en_us_738','en_us_936','en_us_1081','en_us_276','en_us_432','en_us_767','en_us_33','en_us_113'] — each policy kept or created a boundary that produced a high-contradiction short remainder or forced adjacent head-fragment cuts; the offline target instead moved cuts to preserve minimal meaningful phrases.

edit.target: - Is a subordinating relation unresolved at the cut
edit.text: If demoting a boundary because its remainder would contradict, do not promote the immediately adjacent boundary when that would create a head-fragment (bare auxiliary/copula/modal, determiner without noun, numeral without unit, or a noun stripped of required postmodifiers); prefer cuts that keep a minimal meaningful phrase intact.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt reflexively avoids cutting near sentence-openers/function words, but for very short latency budgets isolating an initial function word or discourse marker can be beneficial when the remainder is cohesive and non-contradictory.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_936','en_us_738','en_us_360','en_us_113','en_us_845','en_us_1081'] — in each case the offline target added an early short cut (isolating the opener) and achieved higher H_set, showing such cuts are often safe and helpful in ≤3/≤5 bins when the remainder forms a self-contained clause.

edit.text: Allow a cut that isolates a sentence-initial function word or discourse marker when the following piece is a cohesive, self-contained clause and the isolated opener does not by itself assert a proposition that would contradict the remainder.
